title: One winner, several graves
lede: Circuit City was the second-largest electronics chain when it died. Most of the specialist chains it competed with followed it. The one that passed it in the 1990s is still the market leader.

blocks.title: Electronics chains: who is still standing
blocks.subtitle: The headline figure for each, and what became of it.

items.name: Circuit City
items.text: Net sales in fiscal 2008, its last full year. Liquidated in 2009; the name survives on a web shop.[^1][^15][^37]

items.name: Best Buy
items.text: Revenue in fiscal 2026. It was $7.2B in fiscal 1996.[^25][^24]

items.name: CompUSA
items.text: What Systemax paid in January 2008 for its e-commerce business and 16 store leases. The brand was retired with Circuit City’s in 2012.[^23][^22]

items.name: RadioShack
items.text: Filed for Chapter 11 on February 5, 2015. The name has changed hands since.[^27]

items.name: hhgregg
items.text: Filed for Chapter 11 on March 6, 2017. The court approved closing all 132 stores a month later.[^28]

items.name: CarMax (spun off 2002)
items.text: Not a rival but an offspring: the used-car chain Circuit City started in 1993.[^26]

blocks.source: Company filings as cited. Sparkline points are selected fiscal years from the sales chart above, plus Best Buy’s fiscal 2026 revenue[^25].

blocks.title: What the founder’s son said
blocks.body: Alan Wurtzel, who ran the company until 1986 and sat on the board until 2001, wrote a book about the collapse. His summary to a Richmond audience in 2012: “After I left, my successors became very focused on the bottom line.” The company refused to sell video games because the margin was low, he said, while “Best Buy was happily catering to that market.”[^32][^29]
